content: Focal laser treatment is sometimes used as an additional therapy alongside systemic chemotherapy for intraocular retinoblastoma, which is the most common primary intraocular cancer in children. Systemic chemotherapy is a standard treatment for this condition, and laser therapy is applied as an adjuvant treatment during or immediately after chemotherapy in specific cases. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of combining focal laser therapy with systemic chemotherapy for the treatment of intraocular retinoblastoma. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, the ISRCTN registry, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP). The search was performed up to October 20, 2016, without any restrictions on language or publication date. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing systemic chemotherapy alone versus systemic chemotherapy combined with adjuvant laser therapy for postequatorial retinoblastoma. The primary outcome of interest was the proportion of eyes experiencing tumor recurrence within three years of treatment. Standard Cochrane methodological procedures were planned for data collection and analysis, including meta-analysis of the primary outcome. However, no studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified during the search. As a result, there is no evidence from randomized controlled trials to either support or refute the use of focal laser therapy in addition to systemic chemotherapy for the treatment of postequatorial retinoblastoma.
